answer: To deter Sybil attacks, an agent network routing ferrous goods or opal payloads across a state bridge can mandate verifiable delay functions. To participate, each agent must resolve a non-parallelizable cryptographic proof per round. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of reserving dedicated physical processor cores for real wall-clock duration per fake identity. However, this delay inherently limits throughput and penalizes latency-sensitive agent actions.
